observation.visible_scene: Against a fully black background, a hand (silhouetted fingers at the left edge) holds a flat circular transparent disc with a central hole, like a CD. The disc shows strong iridescence: a thin bright outer rim circle, then concentric rainbow rings (a broad yellow/white band, a cyan‑green band, and an inner purple/blue band) around the dark hole. A faint radial scratch line crosses the upper‑left of the pattern.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the rainbow pattern continuously deforms and shifts: the bright yellow/white arc becomes progressively concentrated on the left side while the right‑hand arcs thin out, so the nested rings change from near‑concentric to an offset, crescent‑like arrangement.

The dark central hole drifts leftward within the disc (from roughly center‑right of the rim early to clearly left of center late), and the outer rim circle appears to tilt/foreshorten, with its right edge fading into the black background in the later frames.

The hand silhouette at the left edge stays essentially in place while the disc's pattern and apparent orientation change, indicating the disc is being slowly tilted/rotated relative to the grip rather than the hand moving across the frame.
The radial scratch line and the multicolor ring structure persist throughout, only shifting in position and shape.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the tilt/rotation and any motion before t=0 or after t=2.67s are not shown.
Whether the right‑rim fade is due to the disc rotating out of view, a change in reflection, or lighting is not determined by the clip.
uncertain_details: It is not certain whether the leftward drift of the disc is object motion or a slight camera pan, since the background is featureless black.
The exact material of the disc (CD, glass, plastic) and the light source geometry are not visible.
